title: DSP, from First Principles to the Optical Link
tagline: A diagram-first course in digital signal processing. Every idea is drawn before it is derived, every chapter ends where it is actually used: inside a coherent optical modem.

pages.title: The domain
pages.summary: What this blog is about, and the shape of the problem the whole course aims at: turning light into bits at rates where the arithmetic is the design.

pages.title: Vision and Research
pages.summary: What I am trying to build, what I am reading and measuring, and the questions I do not have answers to yet.

parts.title: Signals, Sampling and Number Systems
parts.blurb: Before any transform, before any filter, there is a physical quantity and a decision about how often to look at it. Almost every bug in a real DSP chain is a decision from this part, made badly.

articles.title: What a Signal Actually Is
articles.summary: Continuous time versus discrete time, the domain and range of a signal, and the mental model that makes every later chapter obvious.

articles.title: Sampling and Aliasing
articles.summary: The Nyquist-Shannon theorem derived from a picture, why an alias is indistinguishable from a real tone, and how anti-alias filtering saves the day.

articles.title: Quantization, SNR and ENOB
articles.summary: An ideal 12-bit ADC does not give you 12 bits. Where the 6.02N + 1.76 formula comes from, and what actually eats it.

articles.title: Decibels and Dynamic Range
articles.summary: Why engineers think in logs, the 3 dB and 6 dB rules you will use weekly, and how to keep dBm, dBW and dBFS straight.

parts.title: The Frequency Domain
parts.blurb: The Fourier transform is not a trick. It is the statement that a signal can be built out of sinusoids, and the machinery for doing that bookkeeping fast enough to run in real time.

articles.title: From Fourier Series to the Fourier Transform
articles.summary: Harmonics, the periodicity trap, and how letting the period go to infinity turns a sum into an integral.

articles.title: The DFT, Without Magic
articles.summary: What the DFT actually computes, why it is periodic in both domains, and how to read a bin index as a frequency in hertz.

articles.title: The FFT: How It Got Fast
articles.summary: Radix-2 decomposition, the butterfly, and the bit-reversal that everyone gets wrong once. Includes the cost table that explains why 5G and 800G both live on FFTs.

articles.title: Windows, Leakage and Resolution
articles.summary: Why a pure sine leaves a smear, why rectangular is sometimes correct, and how to choose a window from its sidelobe roll-off instead of superstition.

articles.title: The z-Transform and the Unit Circle
articles.summary: The DFT is the z-transform sampled on a circle. This one picture unifies filters, stability and the frequency response.

parts.title: LTI Systems and Filter Design
parts.blurb: Linear time-invariant systems are the only class of systems we can fully solve on paper, which is exactly why almost every real receiver is engineered to stay inside that class.

articles.title: Convolution, and Why Every DSP Block Is One
articles.summary: Flip, shift, multiply, sum - then the same operation as a polynomial product, and as a matrix. Three views of one idea.

articles.title: Poles, Zeros and Stability
articles.summary: Reading a filter off its pole-zero plot, the region of convergence, and the exact condition that separates a filter from an oscillator.

articles.title: FIR Filter Design
articles.summary: Windowed-sinc, least squares and Parks-McClellan, with the linear-phase condition that makes FIRs the default in hardware.

articles.title: IIR Filter Design
articles.summary: The bilinear transform, frequency pre-warping, and the Butterworth/Chebyshev/Bessel trade-off between sharpness, ripple and phase.

articles.title: Phase, Group Delay and Why They Cost You
articles.summary: Two filters can share a magnitude response and behave completely differently. Group delay, phase distortion and all-pass equalisation.

parts.title: Multirate DSP
parts.blurb: The single biggest efficiency win available in any real system: stop processing samples you are about to throw away.

articles.title: Decimation and Interpolation
articles.summary: Rate change done naively, why it aliases, and the anti-imaging and anti-aliasing filters that make it correct.

articles.title: Polyphase Decomposition and Arbitrary Resampling
articles.summary: The noble identity, why a polyphase filter costs the same as a single phase of it, and how to resample by any rational ratio.

articles.title: CIC and Half-Band Filters
articles.summary: Multiplier-free decimation for the front end and the symmetric trick that halves the cost of every factor of two.

parts.title: Statistical and Adaptive DSP
parts.blurb: Real signals are random, the channel is unknown, and it drifts with temperature. This is where DSP stops being a filter and becomes an estimator.

articles.title: Random Signals, Autocorrelation and PSD
articles.summary: Why a random signal has no Fourier transform yet a perfectly well-defined spectrum, and how to estimate one honestly.

articles.title: Matched Filtering and the Wiener Filter
articles.summary: Maximising SNR against minimising MSE - two different optimality criteria, two different filters, and when each is the right one.

articles.title: LMS, RLS and Adaptive Equalisation
articles.summary: The steepest-descent picture, convergence versus misadjustment, and why the sign-sign LMS variant is the one that ships in silicon.

articles.title: Kalman Filtering for Tracking and Recovery
articles.summary: Recursive Bayesian estimation in five equations, and how the same structure reappears as a carrier tracking loop.

parts.title: Communications DSP
parts.blurb: Everything so far, aimed at one goal: given a noisy and distorted analogue waveform, decide which of a finite set of symbols was sent, and do it at hundreds of gigabaud.

articles.title: Pulse Shaping and the Nyquist Criterion
articles.summary: Zero ISI at the sampling instants, the raised-cosine family, and why the root-raised-cosine is split across transmitter and receiver.

articles.title: Eye Diagrams, ISI and the Channel
articles.summary: Reading a link's health from a picture, and the relationship between eye closure, BER and the equaliser you need.

articles.title: PAM and QAM Constellations
articles.summary: Mapping bits to amplitude, Gray coding, and the SNR gap between PAM4 and PAM3 on the same channel.

articles.title: Timing Recovery
articles.summary: The Gardner and Mueller-Muller detectors, why a baud-rate loop is not enough, and how timing error becomes an FFE tap.

articles.title: Carrier Recovery and PLL Design
articles.summary: Phase detectors, loop filters and the lock/acquisition trade-off, with the second-order loop equations you actually need.

parts.title: IEEE Ethernet, Measured
parts.blurb: Ethernet is the largest deployed population of the signal integrity problem: a standards body hands you a channel, a loss budget, a mask and a maximum error ratio, and every DSP idea in this course has to show up on a compliance report. This part takes the theory out of the notebook and onto the bench, in the order an engineer meets it.

articles.title: Six Generations of Ethernet, and the Data-Processing View
articles.summary: From a shared coax bus with collision detection to 800G over eight lanes: what the physical layer added each time the channel ran out of margin, and the four steps every Ethernet generation actually performs.

articles.title: Gain, Loss and the Ethernet Link Budget
articles.summary: What gain means once the channel is a 100-metre cable: insertion loss in dB against frequency, the Nyquist frequency that decides what the equaliser must supply, and the margin arithmetic a link is signed off on.

articles.title: Reading an Eye Diagram
articles.summary: How a persistence trace is built, what eye height and eye width actually measure, why NRZ has one eye and PAM4 has three, and how to read a mask test without memorising it.

articles.title: BERT, BER and the FEC Contract
articles.summary: The measurement that justifies everything else: PRBS patterns, the bathtub curve, the Q-factor behind the numbers, and the pre-FEC error ratio a Reed-Solomon code is allowed to see.

articles.title: The FFT and DFT in Ethernet Compliance
articles.summary: The DFT is not a chapter you leave behind, it is the instrument: bin index to hertz, the transmit spectral mask, the equaliser response, and S-parameters pulled back into the time domain.

articles.title: Compliance Test in Practice
articles.summary: A full nine-step procedure for a 1000BASE-T and 10GBASE-KR port, four ways to get a wrong answer with a correct instrument, and a symptom-to-cause table for when the eye will not open.

parts.title: Optical DSP
parts.blurb: The application. Coherent and IM-DD optical links put every previous chapter in series, at 100+ GBd, in fixed point, in a chip that must not exceed a power budget. This is the part I work in.

articles.title: The Coherent Optical Receiver: A DSP Pipeline Tour
articles.summary: From the 90-degree hybrid to decoded bits, block by block, with the sample-rate and resolution budget for each stage.

articles.title: The 90-Degree Hybrid and I/Q Imbalance
articles.summary: How optics produces a complex baseband signal, and how a 1% quadrature error becomes an image that costs you 30 dB of margin.

articles.title: Chromatic Dispersion and the Frequency-Domain Equaliser
articles.summary: Dispersion as an all-pass phase curve, why time-domain equalisation loses to overlap-save FFT, and the block-size maths that decides it.

articles.title: Polarization Demultiplexing with CMA
articles.summary: Two signals arrive mixed by an unknown 2x2 unitary matrix. The constant-modulus algorithm untangles them blind.

articles.title: Carrier Phase Estimation
articles.summary: Laser linewidth turns a constellation into a ring. Viterbi-Viterbi, blind phase search, and the block-length trade-off between noise and tracking.

articles.title: Fibre Nonlinearity and Digital Backpropagation
articles.summary: The Kerr effect, the split-step method, and the brutal complexity wall that keeps most nonlinear compensation out of the product.

articles.title: PAM4 DSP for IM-DD and Active Electrical Cables
articles.summary: The short-reach chain: FFE, DFE, MLSE and PLL for 100G-per-lane PAM4 over copper and directly detected optics.

parts.title: SerDes for Optical Modules
parts.blurb: A coherent DSP never touches the fibre directly. It is reached through 100-gigabit serial lanes -- host side and line side -- and a great many of an optical module's hard problems live on those lanes rather than in the equaliser. This part is the electrical interface between the DSP and the optics: channel, equalisation, clock recovery, jitter, and the error budget that binds them.

articles.title: The SerDes in an Optical Module
articles.summary: The two electrical edges of a module, retimed versus gearbox architectures, and why an optical DSP's first design decision is how many serial lanes it faces.

articles.title: The Anatomy of a 100G Lane
articles.summary: Serializer to driver on the transmit side, CTLE to slicer on the receive side, and the four processing steps of the Ethernet part reappearing at chip scale.

articles.title: SerDes Channels and the Link Budget
articles.summary: Insertion loss and crosstalk at 26 GHz, how lane density sets the interference, and the channel operating margin arithmetic that replaces a hand-waved budget.

articles.title: SerDes Equalisation
articles.summary: CTLE, transmit FFE, receive FFE and DFE, what each one costs, and why a real link uses all four at once rather than choosing between them.

articles.title: Clock Recovery and Jitter
articles.summary: The CDR loop, phase detectors, and the decomposition of jitter into random and deterministic parts -- the measurement that decides how much eye is left.

articles.title: FEC, Burst Errors and the End-to-End Error Budget
articles.summary: How errors arrive at a SerDes end, why DFE error propagation makes them bursty, and how interleaving and code choice budget a module's whole link.

parts.title: Making It Real
parts.blurb: An algorithm that is not implementable at rate and within power is not an algorithm, it is a paper. Fixed point, silicon architecture and the machine-learning boundary.

articles.title: Fixed-Point DSP, Q-Formats and CORDIC
articles.summary: Choosing a Q-format, predicting overflow before the lab finds it, and computing sin, cos and magnitude without a multiplier.

articles.title: FFT Hardware Architectures
articles.summary: Memory-based, pipelined and parallel FFTs, the twiddle-factor storage problem, and how block floating point buys back dynamic range.

articles.title: Neural Equalisation and the ML/DSP Boundary
articles.summary: Where a small network genuinely beats a DFE, how it is quantised onto the same datapath, and where it does not pay for itself.
